- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; reduce slope of forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment shifts from neutral to positive, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in first 2–3 forecast steps.  
- If model shows steady upward drift with no sentiment signal, it overestimates; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if price drops below 10% of recent 5-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average to reduce lag error.
